  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

messages.content:
你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

- Introduces WorldCrafter, a video world model featuring an implicit 3D-aware memory mechanism that encodes historical frames into a compact representation to preserve spatial-temporal context within a fixed token budget.
- Integrates this memory into camera-controllable autoregressive video generation, achieving a 47.6% improvement in revisit consistency and enhanced camera-control accuracy compared to the strongest baseline.

## Problem and Motivation
Existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often struggle with multi-hop question answering due to the limitations of flat semantic search spaces. Conventional dense retrieval fails to model relationships between intermediate entities, while graph-based RAG methods suffer from unconstrained probability diffusion. This lack of topological control allows lexically similar but logically disconnected distractors to overshadow critical evidence, leading to semantic drift and the retrieval of spurious subgraphs.

## Methodology
ISO-RAG introduces a geometry-aware framework that embeds document networks into hyperbolic space using the Poincaré ball model to better capture hierarchical structures. The core innovation is an isoperimetric control mechanism that acts as a structural filter. By computing a numerically stable, node-wise proxy for the isoperimetric constant, the system explicitly identifies and severs incompatible edges connected to dense generic hubs before propagation. This prunes misleading connections, ensuring that Personalized PageRank diffusion is anchored to query-aligned seeds and restricted to a compact, geometrically bounded local subgraph.

## Results and Contributions
Extensive evaluations demonstrate that ISO-RAG achieves a favorable balance between retrieval efficiency and downstream QA performance. The framework delivers robust average absolute gains of nearly 10% in Recall@5 and 4.3% in Exact Match over competitive baselines. By transforming global diffusion into local, noise-controlled propagation, ISO-RAG effectively mitigates topological noise, providing a rigorous mathematical bound for pruning the search space that heuristic-based graph RAG systems lack.

你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 120 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
PredActor: Predictive Action Diffusion for Steerable Onboard Humanoid Control

Abstract
Diffusion models offer flexible motion generation, but translating this flexibil- ity into feedback-responsive humanoid control remains challenging. Hierarchical systems steer motion through references that may exceed a separate tracker’s ca- pabilities, leaving recovery and physical execution largely to the tracker. Action- only diffusion generates actions directly but lacks an explicit future-state trajec- tory for test-time motion objectives. Joint state–action diffusion provides this rep- resentation, yet representative controllers often depend on privileged full-body states, and support for learned behavior selection and test-time motion steering remains fragmented. We present PredActor, a predictive action diffusion pol- icy that brings these complementary steering capabilities into one directly exe- cuted policy using proprioceptive observations. Conditioned on proprioceptive history and optional task context, PredActor jointly generates executable actions and an internal future-state trajectory. Classifier-free guidance strengthens text-

Write only the summary.

- PredActor is a predictive action diffusion policy designed for steerable onboard humanoid control, addressing the limitations of hierarchical systems and action-only diffusion models.
- It jointly generates executable actions and an internal future-state trajectory, providing an explicit representation for test-time motion objectives that action-only methods lack.
- The policy operates using only proprioceptive observations, eliminating the dependency on privileged full-body states often required by representative joint state-action controllers.
- By integrating complementary steering capabilities into a single directly executed policy, PredActor supports learned behavior selection and robust physical execution.
- The system utilizes classifier-free guidance to enhance performance, conditioned on proprioceptive history and optional task context for flexible motion generation.

  参数:

  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10

  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

    session_id (string): , 默认: default

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

  参数:

    force (boolean): , 默认: False

  参数:

    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

Out-of-Distribution Generalisation with Sequence Models in Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

Abstract
Generalising to unseen tasks remains a fundamental challenge in offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). In this work, we present a principled analysisSep of zero-shot task generalisation in the offline setting and conduct an extensive 3 empirical investigation into the scaling behaviour governing task diversity, dataset size, and network capacity. To facilitate this study, we extend offline sequence modelling architectures to handle multi-task observation and action spaces along- side variable agent counts across tasks. Our primary finding is that scaling task diversity—rather than sheer dataset size—is the dominant factor in achieving ro- bust zero-shot transfer. Through large-scale experiments across four challenging environments (Connector, RWARE, SMAX, and LBF), we demonstrate that our[cs.LG] multi-task approach achieves a mean improvement of 3.2x on held-out test tasks compared to single-task models and consistently outperforms strong behaviour cloning baselines. These results suggest that the development of generalisable MARL agents should prioritise the diversity of the training distribution with varying numbers of agents, providing a roadmap for scaling offline MARL effectively.

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10

  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default

    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.

    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']

    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
SocioVerse2: A Longitudinal Dynamic Social Simulation Framework under a Human-AI Co-evolutionary Paradigm

Abstract
Social simulation offers the social sciences an experimental instrument that the real world cannot
supply, and generative agents have transformed it by acting as silicon samples that unite agent-based[cs.CL] modeling with real behavioral data. Existing platforms verify collective behavior, align simulated
populations with real societies in cross-sections, and employ autonomous agents for the research
process. However, two social science requirements remain without systematic support: intervention
in the content of a simulation and the researcher’s control over the process that produces it. We
present SOCIOVERSE2, which extends SOCIOVERSE 1.0 into a human-AI co-evolutionary paradigm
built from two loops and one infrastructure. The longitudinal simulation loop simulates the target
population with evolving environments and forks counterfactual branches via interventions. The
controllable research loop takes the study itself as an editable state and updates state versions via
controllable editing. The social science agentic infrastructure carries both loops through composable
skills with researcher checkpoints, a population service over five persona pools, and an environment
service over 21 real-world signal sources with point-in-time guarantees. We validate SOCIOVERSE2
across three case families and seven case studies, from reproducing canonical agent-based models
to modeling policy processes on real records and nowcasting macro-economic indices beyond the
response model’s knowledge cutoff. With the human-AI co-evolutionary paradigm, these cases
go beyond system demonstrations to become substantive studies that investigate frontier questions
in their respective disciplines. Code, data services, and a workbench are released as open-sourcearXiv:2609.24911v1 resources.

*Equal contribution.
†Corresponding authors.
This work was completed during the research period at Shanghai Innovation Institute.

Multi-robot systems have shown increasing via- bility in construction due to their ability to execute high- precision actions while reducing human exposure to hazardous tasks. We demonstrate the success of our framework on the construction of a post-and-lintel structure using one robot arm as a timber gripper, and a second robot as a nail-21 fastener. Fig. 1. You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a tldr summary in at most 60 words.

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
Rare Event Estimation via Iterative Unalignment

Abstract
As agents are deployed with increased autonomy, even extremely rare events along their
stochastic output trajectories can occur and prove catastrophic. Safe deployment therefore does
not depend on whether these events can occur, but on how often they might. We study the problem
of estimating the probability of rare events that arise from stochastic variation in the agent’s own
actions. Estimating this type of risk requires searching over the combinatorially vast space of
trajectories. Naive Monte Carlo is computationally prohibitive in this regime, and constructing2026
effective importance sampling (IS) proposals requires coordinated changes to a context-dependent
chain of conditional distributions. We develop a new IS method that perturbs the original
model’s weights to construct the proposal. The proposal is itself a differentiably parameterizedSep
language model, enabling gradient-based search over weight space. We formulate an objective
that combines a differentiable surrogate for event amplification and an adaptive regularization21
scheme that dynamically balances amplification against estimator stability. We evaluate our
approach on ∼120M and ∼2.6B models across three event families spanning 300+ rare events as
rare as 10−9, with reference probabilities computed with < 10% relative standard error. In our
most verifiable settings, we observe that our IS estimator achieves over 800× compute-weighted
efficiency gains over naive Monte Carlo for events with probabilities lower than 10−7. Our
implementation is available at https://github.com/namkoong-lab/iterative-unalignment.[cs.LG]

Write only the summary.

This paper introduces an iterative unalignment method for rare event estimation in stochastic agents, using differentiable weight perturbations to construct importance sampling proposals that achieve over 800x efficiency gains over naive Monte Carlo for events with probabilities below 10^-7.

predictions, latent-space structure, and interpretability analyses suggests that uncertainty can be transformed
into an explicit and measurable component of archaeological inference, providing a robust, transparent, and
reproducible approach to decoding ancient rock art.

  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

- translate_arxiv_pdf 是异步任务，调用后会立即返回 task_id 和 PENDING 状态。
- 翻译进度由前端通过 SSE 实时推送，你不需要也不应该轮询检查翻译状态。

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 250 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Passthrough Rigidity: The Behavioral and Visuomotor Costs of Mediated Perception

Abstract
Broad public adoption of head-mounted displays using video passthrough remains elusive despite significant market investment. A precise understanding of why users experience persistent discomfort even as hardware factors such as resolution[cs.HC] and latency have dramatically improved remains an open issue. This paper investigates the impact of viewing the world through video passthrough systems on human behavioral and physiological patterns through a large-scale multimodal study. We developed a novel protocol to capture synchronized oculomotor, kinematic, and physiological data during a block assembly task requiring complex hand-eye coordination (Figure 1). Using a within-subject design (N=110), we evaluated both natural and passthrough viewing conditions. Our results reveal a four-fold suppression of rotational head velocity and a pronounced decoupling of head-gaze coordination. This suggests motor caution being employed as an adaptive strategy – which we term “Passthrough Rigidity”. This phenomenon appears to shift the information-gathering burden to the oculomotor system, resulting in significantly longer fixation durations and restricted visual search patterns. These kinematic shifts directly correlate with poorer task performance and measurable physiological cost, evidenced by a significant reduction in blink duration and increased reports of ocular strain and cognitive load. We conclude that current passthrough implementations induce a measurable shift from flexible exploration to motor caution, where task performance is preserved at the cost of user comfort and biomechanical efficiency. These findings provide a novel quantitative framework for evaluating and improving future XR devices, establishing that resolving “comfort” for passthrough requires addressing the deep-seated biomechanical compensations caused by mediated perception. All data is made publicly available at https://data.nvision.eecs.yorku.ca/Passthrough/.

Write only the summary.

- This study investigates the persistent discomfort associated with video passthrough head-mounted displays by examining how mediated perception affects human behavioral and physiological patterns, addressing a critical gap in understanding user experience despite hardware improvements.
- Through a large-scale within-subject experiment (N=110) using a novel protocol to capture synchronized oculomotor, kinematic, and physiological data during a complex hand-eye coordination task, the researchers compared natural viewing conditions against passthrough viewing.
- The results identify a phenomenon termed “Passthrough Rigidity,” characterized by a four-fold suppression of rotational head velocity and a pronounced decoupling of head-gaze coordination, indicating that users adopt motor caution as an adaptive strategy to navigate the mediated environment.
- This shift in motor behavior places a significant burden on the oculomotor system, leading to longer fixation durations and restricted visual search patterns, which directly correlate with poorer task performance and measurable physiological costs such as reduced blink duration and increased ocular strain.
- The findings conclude that current passthrough systems force a trade-off where task performance is preserved at the expense of user comfort and biomechanical efficiency, providing a quantitative framework for future XR device development that must address these deep-seated biomechanical compensations.

  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值

    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1

    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
Online Change-point Detection for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

Abstract
Abstract. Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) sys-2026 tems rely on past experience for learning coordinated behaviour, but this experience may become unreliable if the environment or task objective changes during training. In such cases, agents first need a way to recog-Sep nize that the situation has changed before deciding how to adapt. This 4 paper studies online change-point detection for cooperative MARL using reward-derived signals. We propose Patterns of Past Rewards (PPR), a lightweight algorithm-agnostic detector that smooths agents’ return streams, highlights recent changes, and applies a statistical drift detector to flag significant shifts. We evaluate PPR in a custom Speaker-Listener environment based on the Multi-Agent Particle Environment under two controlled non-stationarity scenarios. Our results show a trade-off be-[cs.MA] tween detection speed and alarm stability. A smoothed-return baseline detects earlier but produces many repeated alarms. In contrast, apply- ing the detector directly to raw returns often misses the shift. PPR of- fers a more balanced approach by limiting redundant detections while still identifying the controlled shifts. These findings highlight PPR as a lightweight, reward-based monitoring tool that enables cooperative MARL systems to reliably identify major changes during training.

- The paper introduces Dependency-Aware Revocable Decoding (DARD), a framework designed to address a critical flaw in existing revocable decoding methods for diffusion large language models (dLLMs). Previous approaches often fail because they use unreliable, recently decoded tokens as context when verifying other tokens, leading to conflicting verification signals and unnecessary remasking of valid tokens.
- DARD mitigates this issue by implementing a selective verification context that excludes unreliable tokens. It distinguishes between three token states: masked (M) for undecoded tokens, candidate (C) for decoded but uncertain tokens, and unmasked (U) for high-confidence tokens. This structure ensures that verification is based on a more reliable subset of the context.
- The method employs a confidence-ordered mechanism where each candidate token attends only to unmasked tokens and higher-confidence candidate tokens. This design mimics multi-step decoding, treating higher-confidence candidates as if they were decoded earlier, thereby preventing low-confidence tokens from corrupting the verification process for other positions.
- DARD further optimizes the decoding process by using verification results to estimate the reliability of the candidate set and adaptively controlling how strongly masked tokens rely on candidate tokens. This adaptive control enhances the efficiency of the generation process by dynamically adjusting dependencies based on real-time confidence assessments.
- Extensive experiments across 12 textual and multimodal benchmarks on three open-source dLLMs demonstrate that DARD consistently improves the speed-quality Pareto frontier. Notably, on the Flickr30K dataset, DARD achieves a 2.71× speedup while improving the CIDEr score by 4.35 points compared to the Saber baseline, highlighting the importance of a reliable verification context for effective dLLM inference.

CoRe-MARL: Cooperative Redistribution Under Unknown Dynamics Using Recurrent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

Abstract
Emergency management assistance programs, such as relief distribution, are
essential for delivering necessary supplies to affected communities. However,
these programs operate in a decentralized network of local centers that face
uncertain local demand and supply dynamics, resulting in inconsistent avail-
ability of local services. Redistribution of supplies among these local centers[cs.LG] reduces these imbalances, but the centers often make decisions independently,
with limited information and disrupted transportation. This study develops
CoRe-MARL, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) frame-
work, by formulating a decentralized partially observable Markov decision pro-
cess (Dec-POMDP). We treat each center as an agent that learns a redistribu-
tion policy to improve the service in the worst-case region and reduce the service
gap across regions while protecting network-wide service. We incorporate a re-
current network that captures evolving supply and demand dynamics without
direct observation, while multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO)
enables centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE). We evaluate
the framework in a simulated environment with diverse trajectories, where ex-
act dynamics are not observed by actors and the MAPPO critic. We compare
the recurrent MAPPO with the recurrent independent PPO (IPPO) and a local-
only heuristic, and find that MAPPO reduces the service gap across local centers
and enhances service for the worst-served center while maintaining competitivearXiv:2609.18639v1
network-wide service. The recurrent MAPPO also shows consistent performance
across diverse trajectory patterns, demonstrating its ability to adapt to evolv-
ing dynamics. The findings demonstrate the capability of cooperative learning
for decentralized redistribution and improving equitable service under uncertain

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4

    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10

  参数:

    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1

    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
Generating Chest X-Ray Counterfactuals by Specialising Foundation Image Models

Abstract
AbstractSep 21 Counterfactuallooked under retrospective,image generationhypotheticalanswersscenarios.questions Recentabout howmethodsa subjecthavewouldimprovedhave perceptual quality, identity preservation and faithfulness to an underlying causal model, but their adoption in healthcare is limited by scarce annotated data, distribu- tion shift between datasets, and mismatches between pretrained generative models and those required for counterfactual inference. We propose specialisation, a data and parameter-efficient framework for adapting pretrained, non-causal generative models into causal mechanisms under distribution shift. Based on this framework,[cs.CV] we train a radiology counterfactual image generation model, called RadCF, using latent flow matching. We validate our approach on three chest X-ray datasets span- ning different dataset shifts, data volumes, and counterfactual questions, associated with challenging, highly-localised interventions. Our results show that RadCF and specialisation improve counterfactual soundness over existing methods while being data and parameter efficient, and that the resulting counterfactuals can detect and mitigate shortcut learning in a downstream medical classifier.     paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Learning Beyond What Humans Can Demonstrate

Abstract
Behavior cloning for robot manipulation relies on expert demonstra- tions. However, for tasks that require dynamic stability, precise contact timing, or dexterous coordination, human operators may find it hard or even impossible to collect data. We study this infeasible-demonstration regime and propose GLIDE: Guardrails for Learning from Infeasible Demonstrations Efficiently, a framework that infers task-specific failure modes and converts them into executable guardrails2026 for data collection and policy deployment. Given a task description and the con- ditioning teleoperation code, GLIDE writes guardrails that use system states to filter teleoperation and policy commands, constrain failure-prone actions, and it-Sep eratively improve from trajectory feedback. Across three tasks, GLIDE discov- 21 ersing emergentdata collectionguardrailsoverthatnaivego VRbeyondteleoperationdomain-expertand domain-experthardcoded ones,hardcodedimprov- guardrails. After refinement, GLIDE raises data-collection success from 0–10% to 70–90% across the three tasks. During policy execution, mixed-data guarded policies reach 70%, 60%, and 60% success on Tomato plate transfer, Marker han- dover & stand, and Wine serving tasks. These results show that GLIDE can sup- port policy learning when direct demonstrations are infeasible. Project website:[cs.RO] http://guardrail-policy.github.io/.

Write only the summary.

- Addresses the infeasible-demonstration regime in robot manipulation where human operators cannot provide expert data due to dynamic stability or dexterity constraints.
- Proposes GLIDE, a framework that infers task-specific failure modes and converts them into executable guardrails for both data collection and policy deployment.
- Automatically generates guardrails from task descriptions and teleoperation code to filter commands, constrain failure-prone actions, and iteratively improve via trajectory feedback.
- Discovers emergent data collection guardrails that outperform naive teleoperation and domain-expert hardcoded methods.
- Significantly improves performance, raising data-collection success from 0–10% to 70–90% and achieving 60–70% success on complex tasks like tomato plate transfer and wine serving.

    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1

    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 60 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness

Abstract
2026 Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal sharedSep harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: 21 usinginto modela domain-weights,or instance-optimizedso that its gains surviveharnessunderas training-timea single fixedguidancetargetandharness.transferringThe challengethe behaviorsis thatit theinducestwo harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimized harness cannot serve directly as supervision for the target one. We introduce HARNESS-ZERO, which enables harness distillation through agent-as-harness. Guided by the optimized harness, a harnessing agent corrects student responses before execution in the target harness’s action space, turning harness guidance into training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on the resulting trajectories internalizes harness-induced behavior into the model, so the specialized[cs.AI] harness can be removed at deployment. Our experiments spanning knowledge work, tool use, and science domains show that: ❶For frontier LLMs using the same evolved harness, agent-as-harness outperforms code-as- harness. ❷With the specialized harness removed at deployment, HARNESS-ZERO improves the base model’s macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, even exceeding the 41.7% it reaches with that harness still attached. ❸HARNESS-ZERO recovers harness-induced behaviors absent from the base model, with 82.3% average recovery across 28 patterns in the three domains.

Write only the summary.

- Introduces HARNESS-ZERO, a method to distill specialized agent harness behaviors into model weights for deployment without external harnesses.
- Utilizes an "agent-as-harness" approach to convert optimized harness guidance into training demonstrations within the target action space.
- Improves base model task success from 23.3% to 44.3% across knowledge, tool use, and science domains.
- Recovers 82.3% of harness-induced behaviors, outperforming code-as-harness methods for frontier LLMs.

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 120 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Social Behavior Among Autonomous AI: How Large Language Models Interact in Dynamic Networks

Abstract
Cooperation is a cornerstone of human societies, enabling collective progress in dynamic and uncertain environ-
ments. With the advent of AI systems acting autonomously, it becomes crucial to understand not only human-AI
cooperation but also AI-AI interactions in adaptive networks. In this work, we examine the interactions of AI
using Large Language Models—Mistral, Llama3, Gemma3, and Phi3—in a public goods game within dynamic
network structures. Our experiments were conducted under single-model and mixed-model conditions across
Watts-Strogatz (WS), Barabási-Albert (BA), and Erdős-Rényi (ER) networks. We analyzed the impact of model
architecture, network topology, and prompt design on cooperative behavior. Results show that Mistral and
Llama3 offer high cooperation rates, while Phi3 shows defective tendencies. Additionally, the random structure
of Erdős-Rényi networks dramatically improves cooperation. Prompt design also plays a key role; a society-
benefits prompt leads to a higher cooperation level. These findings offer a preliminary framework for LLM-based
simulations in adaptive social networks.

Keywords
AI & AI Interaction, Large Language Models, Public Goods Game, Dynamic Networks

Write only the summary.

- Investigates AI-AI cooperation using LLMs (Mistral, Llama3, Gemma3, Phi3) in public goods games within dynamic network structures.
- Experiments span single and mixed-model conditions across Watts-Strogatz, Barabási-Albert, and Erdős-Rényi topologies.
- Mistral and Llama3 demonstrate high cooperation rates, whereas Phi3 exhibits defective tendencies.
- Erdős-Rényi network structures significantly enhance cooperative behavior compared to other topologies.
- Prompt design is critical, with society-benefits prompts yielding higher cooperation levels, establishing a framework for LLM-based social simulations.

你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 120 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance

Abstract
Interactive game world models typically autoregress visual observations directly in pixel or latent space, forcing structured properties such as pose, geometry, and occlusion to be implicitly maintained by the same generative sequence. Over long horizons, errors in these latent world properties accumulate, making consistency and controllability fragile. We explicitly model the evolving world state, delegate exact geometric computation to a fixed, zero-parameter renderer, and leave the neural model to synthesize appearance. We instantiate this idea as Marionette, a world model for interactive games with articulated characters, consisting of three components. First, a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model predicts an explicit and interpretable 276-dimensional 3D world state comprising multi-entity articulated skeletons, metric root trajectories, and rotations. Second, a zero-parameter graphics bridge converts the predicted state into pose-control videos, computing world-space geometry and occlusion in closed form. Third, a control-conditioned video-diffusion2026 observation model synthesizes photorealistic RGB observations from the resulting structured controls. Our experiments establish two properties of Marionette. First, the predicted world state is directly controllable. Forcing a mismatched action stream changes root-aligned joint error by 31% acrossAug 48 held-out segments, so the articulated dynamics respond to the actions they are given. Second, long-horizon behaviour is determined in the state, and can be repaired there. Left free, the two 14 generated characters drift to 21.2 m apart (recorded sessions stay near 5 m) and a third of frames show ground penetration. Two rules imposed on the explicit state, a terrain collider and a separation cap, cut penetration by 66% and keep the pair engaged, with no change to the observation model. Routing appearance through the predicted state costs no fidelity we can detect, at an FVD of 831 against 799 for recorded pose. Together, these results show that Marionette provides an explicit and controllable world representation while preserving high-quality visual generation.[cs.CV] Date: August 17, 2026 Project Page: https://alayalab.github.io/Marionette/

Write only the summary.

- Marionette is a world model for interactive games that explicitly predicts a 276-dimensional 3D state, including articulated skeletons and trajectories, to avoid error accumulation in latent space.
- The system uses a zero-parameter graphics bridge to compute exact geometry and occlusion, while a video-diffusion model synthesizes photorealistic RGB observations from these structured controls.
- Experiments demonstrate high controllability, where mismatched actions significantly alter joint error, confirming that dynamics respond directly to input actions.
- Long-horizon stability is improved by applying simple rules to the explicit state, reducing ground penetration by 66% and maintaining character engagement without modifying the observation model.
- The approach preserves visual fidelity, achieving an FVD of 831 compared to 799 for recorded pose, proving that routing appearance through an explicit state does not degrade quality.

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 120 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Who Pays for the KV Cache? Attributing Shared AI Inference Spend Across Kubernetes and LLM Provider Bills

Abstract
Abstract. Organizations pay for AI through disconnected ledgers: Kubernetes allocations for self- hosted inference, gateway logs, and per-token bills from API providers. We present unalloc, an open-source tool that joins OpenCost, LiteLLM, OpenAI and Anthropic cost data into one Decimal- exact ledger and reports the share of spend with no owner, and use it to study where attribution breaks at the seams between these systems. Five case studies run inference for real or simulate it: a vLLM-style serving simulator with paged KV memory and prefix caching; a PyTorch transformer serving a multi-tenant trace with a real KV cache; tensor- and pipeline-parallel inference on torch.distributed; the unmodified CLI against mock provider APIs; and four downstream use cases. At the seams, in a constructed multi-pod deployment scenario — one month of synthetic OpenCost allocations, not observed organizational billing data — owner labels set only on Leader­ WorkerSet leader pods leave 66% of that deployment’s GPU bill unowned, and the natural fallback key assigns 61% of it to a Helm chart name while the headline unallocated share falls to 4%; enabling every source double counts all gateway spend; and reading one page of a billing API reports a quarter of spend. Inside a shared inference server the metering rule decides who pays: on an NVIDIA H100 running vLLM, a token meter assigns a retrieval-heavy tenant 12–14 percentage points more of the bill than an equal time-share meter at every load tested, while GPU utilization reads 97–99% across configured loads of 2 to 16 requests per second (3.7 to 26.9 completed requests per second) and power draw tracks load. Neither meter is a ground truth, and we position these results against recent Shapley-based energy attribution. Code, raw data, captured evidence, figures and this paper regenerate from the repository.

Write only the summary.

- Introduces **unalloc**, an open-source tool that unifies Kubernetes, gateway, and LLM provider cost data into a single Decimal-exact ledger to identify unowned AI inference spend.
- Demonstrates significant attribution failures at system seams, where misconfigured labels leave 66% of GPU bills unowned and fallback keys incorrectly assign 61% to Helm chart names.
- Highlights that enabling all data sources causes double-counting of gateway spend, while partial API reads report only a quarter of actual costs.
- Shows that metering rules drastically impact cost allocation; on NVIDIA H100s, token-based metering assigns 12–14% more cost to retrieval-heavy tenants than time-share metering, despite high GPU utilization.
