This paper introduces LoRA-generating hypernetworks that enable efficient on-device LLM personalization by synthesizing user-specific low-rank adaptations from context tokens, combining the low inference latency of parameter-efficient fine-tuning with the computational feasibility of in-context learning for mobile devices.

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 60 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Feedback Coding Enables Inference-Time Covert Agentic Communication

Abstract
AbstractSep As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate digital interactions, users can leverage LLM-generated text as cover for covert communication within seemingly benign conversations.21 Existing LLM steganography, however, is predominantly white-box, requiring the sender and receiver to share the cover statistics, typically through access to the model weights and prompt. Black-box schemes remove this requirement by allowing the receiver to operate solely on the generated text, but current approaches rely on fixed-length, open-loop watermarking techniques that suffer from high decoding error rates under variable-length token generation. We recast black-box LLM steganography as a sequential[cs.IT] communication problem with causal, noiseless feedback: every generated token is observed by both parties and can guide subsequent embedding. Based on this perspective, we introduce Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), a feedback-coding scheme that combines posterior matching with a decode-and-confirm phase. The design is inspired by classical information-theoretic feedback- coding principles, while its security is established through a cryptographic reduction proof. Across three open-weight language models, we demonstrate that BAM attains 0-0.1% empirical message error on an 8-bit payload in around 50 tokens, across 1000 trials, versus 10-17% for the strongest black-box baseline at comparable length. Building on the proposed steganography algorithm, we demonstrate the feasibility of an end-to-end communication protocol that achieves high communication rates across multiple conversational settings.

Write only the summary.

- Recasts black-box LLM steganography as a sequential communication problem using causal, noiseless feedback.
- Introduces Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), a feedback-coding scheme with cryptographic security guarantees.
- Achieves 0-0.1% message error on 8-bit payloads in ~50 tokens, significantly outperforming baselines.
- Demonstrates an end-to-end protocol for high-rate covert communication across multiple conversational settings.

  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a tldr summary in at most 250 words.

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance

Abstract
Interactive game world models typically autoregress visual observations directly in pixel or latent space, forcing structured properties such as pose, geometry, and occlusion to be implicitly maintained by the same generative sequence. Over long horizons, errors in these latent world properties accumulate, making consistency and controllability fragile. We explicitly model the evolving world state, delegate exact geometric computation to a fixed, zero-parameter renderer, and leave the neural model to synthesize appearance. We instantiate this idea as Marionette, a world model for interactive games with articulated characters, consisting of three components. First, a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model predicts an explicit and interpretable 276-dimensional 3D world state comprising multi-entity articulated skeletons, metric root trajectories, and rotations. Second, a zero-parameter graphics bridge converts the predicted state into pose-control videos, computing world-space geometry and occlusion in closed form. Third, a control-conditioned video-diffusion2026 observation model synthesizes photorealistic RGB observations from the resulting structured controls. Our experiments establish two properties of Marionette. First, the predicted world state is directly controllable. Forcing a mismatched action stream changes root-aligned joint error by 31% acrossAug 48 held-out segments, so the articulated dynamics respond to the actions they are given. Second, long-horizon behaviour is determined in the state, and can be repaired there. Left free, the two 14 generated characters drift to 21.2 m apart (recorded sessions stay near 5 m) and a third of frames show ground penetration. Two rules imposed on the explicit state, a terrain collider and a separation cap, cut penetration by 66% and keep the pair engaged, with no change to the observation model. Routing appearance through the predicted state costs no fidelity we can detect, at an FVD of 831 against 799 for recorded pose. Together, these results show that Marionette provides an explicit and controllable world representation while preserving high-quality visual generation.[cs.CV] Date: August 17, 2026 Project Page: https://alayalab.github.io/Marionette/

Write only the summary.

Marionette introduces a novel interactive game world model that decouples the prediction of explicit, interpretable 3D world states from visual rendering by using a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model to predict articulated character skeletons and trajectories, a zero-parameter graphics bridge to compute exact geometry and occlusion, and a control-conditioned video diffusion model to synthesize photorealistic observations, thereby enabling direct controllability of world properties and significantly reducing long-horizon errors like ground penetration and character drift without sacrificing visual fidelity.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Minimum Time Trajectories for a Car-Like Mobile Robot Moving with Rigid Wheels Under Non-Sliding Constraints

Abstract
Abstract This paper studies the minimum time trajectories of a car-like mobile robot navigating in2026 an obstacle free environment. The robot, with forward and backward speeds, is controlled by bounded front-wheels acceleration and limited front-wheels steering rate. The paper extends previous resultsSep which solved this problem for the kinematic car-like robot. However the kinematic model assumes 21 pure rolling at the wheels ground contacts. This assumption requires non-sliding constraints for the front and rear wheels that can only be handled by the robot dynamics. This paper formulates the non-sliding constraints based on the robot dynamics then augments the kinematic model time-optimal path primitives with three new path primitives associated with the non-sliding constraints. The three non-sliding path primitives together with the kinematic model twelve path primitives form the car-like robot time optimal trajectories. Approximate analytic solutions for the non-sliding path primitives[cs.RO] are also provided. Examples study the time-optimal path primitives along representative maneuvers, illustrating how the non-sliding constraints influence the time optimal trajectories of the car-like robot.

Write only the summary.

- Studies minimum time trajectories for car-like robots with rigid wheels under non-sliding constraints.
- Extends kinematic models by incorporating robot dynamics to handle front and rear wheel constraints.
- Introduces three new path primitives for non-sliding conditions alongside existing kinematic primitives.
- Provides approximate analytic solutions and examples demonstrating the impact on time-optimal maneuvers.

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

## Problem & Approach
This paper introduces "Security Reasoning Topology," a framework modeling LLM reasoning as explicit structural processes (Linear, Branching, Graph) rather than implicit sequences. It maps these topologies to Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Tree-of-Thought (ToT), and Graph-of-Thought (GoT) to analyze cybersecurity tasks.

## Experimental Setup
The study evaluates five LLMs (Llama 2, GPT-5.1, Mistral) across three datasets: MITRE ATT&CK, CTI, and CVE. Topology implementations are controlled via prompt engineering, with fixed decoding parameters to ensure consistent comparison against non-topological baselines like few-shot and RAG.

## Key Findings
Graph-of-Thought (GoT) consistently outperforms other methods, achieving the highest accuracy (e.g., 85.0% on ATT&CK). The results demonstrate that complex, interconnected reasoning structures significantly enhance performance in heterogeneous security analysis tasks compared to linear or branching approaches.

    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）

    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4

    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

The summary must have 3-4 short sections, each starting with a '## ' header.

Paper content:
Minimum Time Trajectories for a Car-Like Mobile Robot Moving with Rigid Wheels Under Non-Sliding Constraints

Abstract
Abstract This paper studies the minimum time trajectories of a car-like mobile robot navigating in2026 an obstacle free environment. The robot, with forward and backward speeds, is controlled by bounded front-wheels acceleration and limited front-wheels steering rate. The paper extends previous resultsSep which solved this problem for the kinematic car-like robot. However the kinematic model assumes 21 pure rolling at the wheels ground contacts. This assumption requires non-sliding constraints for the front and rear wheels that can only be handled by the robot dynamics. This paper formulates the non-sliding constraints based on the robot dynamics then augments the kinematic model time-optimal path primitives with three new path primitives associated with the non-sliding constraints. The three non-sliding path primitives together with the kinematic model twelve path primitives form the car-like robot time optimal trajectories. Approximate analytic solutions for the non-sliding path primitives[cs.RO] are also provided. Examples study the time-optimal path primitives along representative maneuvers, illustrating how the non-sliding constraints influence the time optimal trajectories of the car-like robot.

Write only the summary.

## Problem
Analyzes minimum time trajectories for car-like robots with rigid wheels under non-sliding constraints in obstacle-free environments.

## Method
Extends kinematic models by incorporating robot dynamics to handle non-sliding constraints, augmenting existing path primitives with three new dynamic ones.

## Results
Provides approximate analytic solutions for these new primitives and demonstrates how non-sliding constraints influence time-optimal maneuvers.

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

  参数:

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a tldr summary in at most 250 words.

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
Decoding Guardrails: XAI-Guided Perturbation Analysis of Prompt Injection Detection

Abstract
Abstract. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed inSep production systems, raising concerns about their exposure to adversarial manipulation through prompt injection and jailbreak attacks. Classifier- based guardrails, such as Prompt Guard 2, are widely used as a first21 line of defense against such attacks, but their internal decision logic is largely opaque to both defenders and attackers. This paper presents an exploratory case study that applies explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques to analyze how Prompt Guard 2 distinguishes mali- cious from benign prompts. We conduct four experiments to probe this question empirically. Guided[cs.CR] by Vanilla Gradient and SHAP attributions, we find that Prompt Guard 2’s decisions rely on the cumulative contribution of many tokens rather than a few dominant ones, yet saliency-guided synonym substitution and sentence-level paraphrasing can flip its predictions while altering only a moderate fraction of the text, in some cases yielding a successful jailbreak against the underlying LLM. A dataset-scale saliency analysis further shows that undetected injection prompts systematically lack the lexi- cal markers the classifier relies on. We discuss the implications of these findings for the design and evaluation of classifier-based guardrails, and argue that explanation methods intended to support transparency can simultaneously lower the cost of constructing successful adversarial by- passes.

Write only the summary.

This paper presents an exploratory case study applying explainable AI techniques, specifically Vanilla Gradient and SHAP attributions, to analyze the decision logic of the Prompt Guard 2 classifier for detecting prompt injection attacks, revealing that while the model relies on cumulative token contributions rather than dominant features, it remains vulnerable to saliency-guided synonym substitutions and paraphrasing that can flip predictions and enable successful jailbreaks, thereby demonstrating that transparency-enhancing explanation methods can inadvertently lower the cost of constructing effective adversarial bypasses.

Paper content:
Critical-State RL: Diagnosing Trainable States for Multi-Turn Tool Use

Abstract
Multi-turn tool-use failures can hinge on a single model call, yet reward variation alone Sep does not reveal which call would benefit from training. When rewards depend on later interactions, their variation can reflect downstream randomness rather than differences 21 between the current actions. We introduce Critical-State RL to identify trainable states in multi-turn interactions. Given task-defined candidate calls and local rewards, the method assesses whether each reward captures the action’s effect on task success and whether improvement over a reference policy is possible. It then uses nested sampling to separate action-dependent reward variation from continuation noise and optimizes the policy at the selected states using contextual-bandit training. Experiments on the Berkeley Function[cs.LG] Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) v4 compare training at diagnostic-selected states with training at alternative states. For missing-function tasks, the diagnostic selects the response after the tool becomes available; for missing-argument tasks, it selects the response before the missing argument is supplied. Training the selected responses improves performance, including about 14 percentage points on the missing-function task, while training the alternatives leaves performance flat or worse. We further apply the recipe across models and tasks, including logged repeat-call avoidance and memory management.

Write only the summary.

Critical-State RL identifies trainable states in multi-turn tool use by separating action-dependent reward variation from continuation noise, enabling targeted policy optimization that significantly improves performance on tasks like missing-function handling.

Paper content:
DualWAM: Dual-System World Action Models for Asynchronous Global Planning and Local Refinement

Abstract
World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate robot actions and predict future world states, transferring priors2026 from video pretraining to robot control. However, future visual prediction is computationally expensive, so existing WAMs often rely on long action chunks to amortize inference cost across control steps, at the cost of closed-loop responsiveness.Sep We present DualWAM, a dual-system WAM that preserves broader-horizon world-action generation while 21 enablingperiodicallyhigh-frequencyperforms high-noiseclosed-loopbidirectionalaction updatesdenoisingby decouplingover a broaderglobal world-actionplanning andchunklocal refinement.to establishSystema global2 plan, while wrist-only System 1 extracts a temporally aligned short window from the intermediate denoising state and completes low-noise refinement using the latest wrist observations, which provide action-aligned cues about local geometry, motion, and contact during interaction. The two systems operate asynchronously along a shared denoising trajectory: each global plan is reused across multiple local updates, while System 1 repeatedly incorporates fresh interaction feedback. Across zero-shot manipulation tasks on Franka and Galbot, DualWAM improves success over the strongest[cs.RO] evaluated baseline by 4.5 percentage points on average, while achieving a 16.6× critical-path speedup. Further studies show that role-matched egocentric and UMI data improve success by 14 percentage points, and that the decoupled design naturally supports edge–cloud deployment with substantially lower communication overhead than the baseline. arXiv:2609.24868v1

Write only the summary.

- **Problem and Motivation**: Existing World Action Models (WAMs) face a trade-off between computational cost and responsiveness; they often use long action chunks to amortize the high cost of future visual prediction, which compromises closed-loop reactivity.
- **DualWAM Architecture**: The paper introduces DualWAM, a dual-system framework that decouples global planning from local refinement. System 2 generates a broad-horizon global plan, while System 1 performs high-frequency, low-noise local refinement using a temporally aligned short window and the latest wrist observations for precise interaction cues.
- **Asynchronous Operation**: The two systems operate asynchronously along a shared denoising trajectory. The global plan is reused across multiple local updates, allowing System 1 to repeatedly incorporate fresh interaction feedback without waiting for a new global inference, thus maintaining high-frequency control.
- **Performance and Efficiency**: On zero-shot manipulation tasks with Franka and Galbot robots, DualWAM improves success rates by an average of 4.5 percentage points over the strongest baseline while achieving a 16.6× critical-path speedup.
- **Data and Deployment Benefits**: The study demonstrates that role-matched egocentric and UMI data further boost success by 14 percentage points. Additionally, the decoupled design facilitates efficient edge–cloud deployment with significantly lower communication overhead compared to standard baselines.

    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

Thought: 任务已完成

参数或调用注定失败的工具；请在 Thought 中明确说明无法执行的原因，再用
Action: FINISH 结束。此时不要声称任务已经完成。
注意：只能使用上面列出的工具。每次只能执行一个动作。
强约束：
- Action 后必须是“严格 JSON”(双引号、true/false/null, 小写)
- 禁止 Python 风格 True/False/None
- 禁止尾随逗号、注释、以及任何额外文本
关于“指代上一条操作的论文”：
- 当用户没有给出明确的论文序号/ID/标题，但你判断用户是在指代“最近一次操作过的那篇论文”（例如上下文中的指代性表达），
  则在调用需要论文引用的工具时，把 args 里的 ref 设置为 null(JSON null), 由工具自动定位最近操作的论文。
- 如果用户给出了明确序号/ID/标题，则正常传 ref。
关于异步任务（翻译）：
- translate_arxiv_pdf 是异步任务，调用后会立即返回 task_id 和 PENDING 状态。
- 翻译进度由前端通过 SSE 实时推送，你不需要也不应该轮询检查翻译状态。
- 调用 translate_arxiv_pdf 之后，直接 FINISH 即可，不要再调用 get_paper_cache_status 去查看翻译是否完成。
正确示例：
Action: {"name":"translate_arxiv_pdf","args":{"ref":2,"session_id":"demo1","force":false,"service":"bing","threads":4,"keep_dual":false}}

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a tldr summary in at most 120 words.

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
CoRe-MARL: Cooperative Redistribution Under Unknown Dynamics Using Recurrent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

Abstract
Emergency management assistance programs, such as relief distribution, are
essential for delivering necessary supplies to affected communities. However,
these programs operate in a decentralized network of local centers that face
uncertain local demand and supply dynamics, resulting in inconsistent avail-
ability of local services. Redistribution of supplies among these local centers[cs.LG] reduces these imbalances, but the centers often make decisions independently,
with limited information and disrupted transportation. This study develops
CoRe-MARL, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) frame-
work, by formulating a decentralized partially observable Markov decision pro-
cess (Dec-POMDP). We treat each center as an agent that learns a redistribu-
tion policy to improve the service in the worst-case region and reduce the service
gap across regions while protecting network-wide service. We incorporate a re-
current network that captures evolving supply and demand dynamics without
direct observation, while multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO)
enables centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE). We evaluate
the framework in a simulated environment with diverse trajectories, where ex-
act dynamics are not observed by actors and the MAPPO critic. We compare
the recurrent MAPPO with the recurrent independent PPO (IPPO) and a local-
only heuristic, and find that MAPPO reduces the service gap across local centers
and enhances service for the worst-served center while maintaining competitivearXiv:2609.18639v1
network-wide service. The recurrent MAPPO also shows consistent performance
across diverse trajectory patterns, demonstrating its ability to adapt to evolv-
ing dynamics. The findings demonstrate the capability of cooperative learning
for decentralized redistribution and improving equitable service under uncertain

Keywords: Multi-agent reinforcement learning, Cooperative decision making,

CoRe-MARL is a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that formulates emergency supply redistribution as a Dec-POMDP, utilizing recurrent networks and MAPPO to enable decentralized local centers to learn policies that reduce service gaps and improve worst-case outcomes under unknown, evolving supply and demand dynamics.

content.text: Describe what this figure shows in one or two sentences.
Comparison of model reasoning methods.

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a structured summary in at most 60 words.

The summary must have 3-4 short sections, each starting with a '## ' header.

Paper content:
Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance

Abstract
Interactive game world models typically autoregress visual observations directly in pixel or latent space, forcing structured properties such as pose, geometry, and occlusion to be implicitly maintained by the same generative sequence. Over long horizons, errors in these latent world properties accumulate, making consistency and controllability fragile. We explicitly model the evolving world state, delegate exact geometric computation to a fixed, zero-parameter renderer, and leave the neural model to synthesize appearance. We instantiate this idea as Marionette, a world model for interactive games with articulated characters, consisting of three components. First, a two-stage autoregressive dynamics model predicts an explicit and interpretable 276-dimensional 3D world state comprising multi-entity articulated skeletons, metric root trajectories, and rotations. Second, a zero-parameter graphics bridge converts the predicted state into pose-control videos, computing world-space geometry and occlusion in closed form. Third, a control-conditioned video-diffusion2026 observation model synthesizes photorealistic RGB observations from the resulting structured controls. Our experiments establish two properties of Marionette. First, the predicted world state is directly controllable. Forcing a mismatched action stream changes root-aligned joint error by 31% acrossAug 48 held-out segments, so the articulated dynamics respond to the actions they are given. Second, long-horizon behaviour is determined in the state, and can be repaired there. Left free, the two 14 generated characters drift to 21.2 m apart (recorded sessions stay near 5 m) and a third of frames show ground penetration. Two rules imposed on the explicit state, a terrain collider and a separation cap, cut penetration by 66% and keep the pair engaged, with no change to the observation model. Routing appearance through the predicted state costs no fidelity we can detect, at an FVD of 831 against 799 for recorded pose. Together, these results show that Marionette provides an explicit and controllable world representation while preserving high-quality visual generation.[cs.CV] Date: August 17, 2026 Project Page: https://alayalab.github.io/Marionette/

Write only the summary.

## Problem
Existing game world models struggle with long-horizon consistency due to implicit latent state errors.

## Method
Marionette explicitly predicts 3D world states, uses a zero-parameter renderer for geometry, and applies video diffusion for appearance.

## Results
The model achieves high controllability and reduces ground penetration by 66% via state constraints.

## Impact
It provides an explicit, controllable world representation while maintaining high-fidelity visual generation.

CoRe-MARL: Cooperative Redistribution Under Unknown Dynamics Using Recurrent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

Abstract
Emergency management assistance programs, such as relief distribution, are
essential for delivering necessary supplies to affected communities. However,
these programs operate in a decentralized network of local centers that face
uncertain local demand and supply dynamics, resulting in inconsistent avail-
ability of local services. Redistribution of supplies among these local centers[cs.LG] reduces these imbalances, but the centers often make decisions independently,
with limited information and disrupted transportation. This study develops
CoRe-MARL, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) frame-
work, by formulating a decentralized partially observable Markov decision pro-
cess (Dec-POMDP). We treat each center as an agent that learns a redistribu-
tion policy to improve the service in the worst-case region and reduce the service
gap across regions while protecting network-wide service. We incorporate a re-
current network that captures evolving supply and demand dynamics without
direct observation, while multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO)
enables centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE). We evaluate
the framework in a simulated environment with diverse trajectories, where ex-
act dynamics are not observed by actors and the MAPPO critic. We compare
the recurrent MAPPO with the recurrent independent PPO (IPPO) and a local-
only heuristic, and find that MAPPO reduces the service gap across local centers
and enhances service for the worst-served center while maintaining competitivearXiv:2609.18639v1
network-wide service. The recurrent MAPPO also shows consistent performance
across diverse trajectory patterns, demonstrating its ability to adapt to evolv-
ing dynamics. The findings demonstrate the capability of cooperative learning
for decentralized redistribution and improving equitable service under uncertain

    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

  参数:

    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a tldr summary in at most 250 words.

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
Human-LLM Deliberation as Interactive Proof: Conditions for Verifiability Without Transparency

Abstract
When an LLM supplies an argument that a user could not readily construct, how can the
user decide whether to accept its claim? Inspired by interactive proofs, we model human–
LLM deliberation as an interaction between a prover with unrestricted internal search and
a resource-bounded human verifier. The verifier requests and checks supporting details[cs.CL]
without access to the LLM’s internal state. Passed checks accumulate evidence toward
an acceptance threshold. We prove anytime-valid soundness against adaptive provers: the
probability of ever accepting a false claim is at most a chosen error level, provided the
task supplies bounds on false passes and human checking errors that remain valid after
every relevant history. A finite-horizon completeness bound additionally requires bounds
on the adequacy of honest responses and sufficient diagnostic progress. Further checks can
strengthen the evidence for acceptance, but each requires another adequate response and
reliable human effort. Whether this tradeoff permits certification depends on the verifier’s
effort budget, cognitive load, expertise, and fatigue. We identify conditions under which
the supplied bounds certify a specified sequence of local checks but not a specified global
check under the same resource budgets.
Keywords: Interactive Proofs, Human-AI Decision-Making, Resource-Bounded Verifica-
tion, Verifiability, Human-LLM DeliberationarXiv:2609.24895v1

    force (boolean): , 默认: False

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

- translate_arxiv_pdf 是异步任务，调用后会立即返回 task_id 和 PENDING 状态。

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

请按照ReAct框架的格式思考和行动:
Thought: 分析当前情况和下一步需要做什么
Action: {"name":"工具名称","args":{参数对象}}
Observation: 工具执行的结果
当你认为任务已经完成时，使用以下格式结束：
Thought: 任务已完成
Action: FINISH
如果任务因为缺少必要上下文、参数非法或工具能力不支持而无法执行，不要编造
参数或调用注定失败的工具；请在 Thought 中明确说明无法执行的原因，再用
Action: FINISH 结束。此时不要声称任务已经完成。
注意：只能使用上面列出的工具。每次只能执行一个动作。
强约束：
- Action 后必须是“严格 JSON”(双引号、true/false/null, 小写)
- 禁止 Python 风格 True/False/None
- 禁止尾随逗号、注释、以及任何额外文本
关于“指代上一条操作的论文”：
- 当用户没有给出明确的论文序号/ID/标题，但你判断用户是在指代“最近一次操作过的那篇论文”（例如上下文中的指代性表达），
  则在调用需要论文引用的工具时，把 args 里的 ref 设置为 null(JSON null), 由工具自动定位最近操作的论文。
- 如果用户给出了明确序号/ID/标题，则正常传 ref。
关于异步任务（翻译）：
- translate_arxiv_pdf 是异步任务，调用后会立即返回 task_id 和 PENDING 状态。
- 翻译进度由前端通过 SSE 实时推送，你不需要也不应该轮询检查翻译状态。
- 调用 translate_arxiv_pdf 之后，直接 FINISH 即可，不要再调用 get_paper_cache_status 去查看翻译是否完成。
正确示例：

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 250 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Learning Beyond What Humans Can Demonstrate

Abstract
Behavior cloning for robot manipulation relies on expert demonstra- tions. However, for tasks that require dynamic stability, precise contact timing, or dexterous coordination, human operators may find it hard or even impossible to collect data. We study this infeasible-demonstration regime and propose GLIDE: Guardrails for Learning from Infeasible Demonstrations Efficiently, a framework that infers task-specific failure modes and converts them into executable guardrails2026 for data collection and policy deployment. Given a task description and the con- ditioning teleoperation code, GLIDE writes guardrails that use system states to filter teleoperation and policy commands, constrain failure-prone actions, and it-Sep eratively improve from trajectory feedback. Across three tasks, GLIDE discov- 21 ersing emergentdata collectionguardrailsoverthatnaivego VRbeyondteleoperationdomain-expertand domain-experthardcoded ones,hardcodedimprov- guardrails. After refinement, GLIDE raises data-collection success from 0–10% to 70–90% across the three tasks. During policy execution, mixed-data guarded policies reach 70%, 60%, and 60% success on Tomato plate transfer, Marker han- dover & stand, and Wine serving tasks. These results show that GLIDE can sup- port policy learning when direct demonstrations are infeasible. Project website:[cs.RO] http://guardrail-policy.github.io/.

Write only the summary.

- The paper addresses the "infeasible-demonstration" regime in robot manipulation, where tasks requiring dynamic stability or dexterous coordination are too difficult for human operators to demonstrate effectively, thereby limiting the applicability of standard behavior cloning.
- It introduces GLIDE (Guardrails for Learning from Infeasible Demonstrations Efficiently), a framework that automatically infers task-specific failure modes and converts them into executable guardrails to filter teleoperation and policy commands, constrain failure-prone actions, and iteratively improve based on trajectory feedback.
- GLIDE leverages task descriptions and conditioning teleoperation code to generate emergent data collection guardrails that outperform both naive teleoperation and domain-expert hardcoded constraints, significantly enhancing the quality of collected data.
- Experimental results across three complex tasks (Tomato plate transfer, Marker handover & stand, and Wine serving) show that GLIDE raises data-collection success rates from 0–10% to 70–90%.
- Policies trained on this guarded mixed data achieve 60–70% success rates during execution, demonstrating that GLIDE effectively supports policy learning in scenarios where direct human demonstrations are infeasible.

    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

Paper content:
GAE: Learning a Geometry-Native Latent Space for 3D-Consistent World Generation

Abstract
We present a compact geometry-native latent space as a shared foundation for
perception and generation. Visual generators can produce photorealistic frames
without preserving a consistent 3D scene. We argue that this is not only a mod-arXiv:2609.24981v1
eling problem but also a representation problem: generators typically evolve
appearance-centric latents, while perception models recover geometry in a se-
mantically rich space that encodes cross-view structure. Rather than adding ge-
ometry as another output, we reparameterize a geometry foundation model’s fea-
tures into a compact latent space for generation. We realize this shift with the
geometry-native autoencoder (GAE), whose latent is jointly decodable to appear-
ance, depth, cameras, and point maps. With this state, a standard conditional flow
supports diverse generation tasks. In controlled comparisons that hold the gen-
erator and training protocol fixed, replacing the latent with GAE improves both
visual quality and independently measured 3D coherence: FVD falls by 12.7%
and 23.1% on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, and camera-trajectory error is halved
on RealEstate10K. Together, these results show that the latent space is central to
geometry-consistent generation and can serve as a shared interface between per-
ception and generation.

你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 60 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Learning Physics from an Imperfect Ancestor

Abstract
Neural operators evaluate parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) cheaply
but degrade sharply outside their training distribution. Physics-informed neural
networks (PINNs) avoid dependence on labeled data, yet their optimization can2026 be basin-fragile: when the governing residual admits multiple solutions, a PINN
trained from scratch may converge to a physically incorrect state despite achieving
a small residual. We show that these failure modes can be addressed jointly: anSep imperfect NO provides the structural prior needed to place a PINN in the correct
solution basin, while the PDE residual refines the solution beyond the operator’s
accuracy. We introduce a three-stage framework that freezes the spatial basis of21
a physics-informed NO, extrapolates its solution branch to an out-of-distribution
parameter using a polynomial continuation prior, and distills the resulting field
into a fresh PINN. The NO (teacher) need not be accurate at the target; it transfers
solution-branch information, while PDE residual minimization in the PINN (stu-
dent) governs convergence. We evaluate the framework on three nonlinear PDEs:
1D viscous Burgers, 2D steady Allen–Cahn near a pitchfork bifurcation, and 2D[cs.LG] steady lid-driven cavity flow. For Allen–Cahn, where the trivial solution satis-
fies the PDE residual exactly, a standard PINN consistently collapses to the trivial
zero branch, whereas distillation from the crude extrapolated operator recovers the
non-trivial branch that matches the finite-difference reference. For the lid-driven
cavity, extrapolating to a Reynolds number of Re = 3200 accelerates convergence
to the correct physical state, achieving competitive accuracy using fewer parame-
ters and optimization steps than recent literature baselines. These results establish
a simple principle: an NO need not accurately predict the solution to be useful; it
only needs to identify the correct basin from which PINN optimization can recover
it.

Write only the summary.

- Addresses PINN basin-fragility and neural operator out-of-distribution degradation via a three-stage distillation framework.
- Uses an imperfect neural operator to provide structural priors, guiding PINNs to the correct solution basin.
- Polynomial continuation extrapolates the operator's solution branch to out-of-distribution parameters.
- Demonstrates superior performance on Burgers, Allen–Cahn, and lid-driven cavity flows, recovering non-trivial branches.

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 250 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Online Change-point Detection for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

Abstract
Abstract. Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) sys-2026 tems rely on past experience for learning coordinated behaviour, but this experience may become unreliable if the environment or task objective changes during training. In such cases, agents first need a way to recog-Sep nize that the situation has changed before deciding how to adapt. This 4 paper studies online change-point detection for cooperative MARL using reward-derived signals. We propose Patterns of Past Rewards (PPR), a lightweight algorithm-agnostic detector that smooths agents’ return streams, highlights recent changes, and applies a statistical drift detector to flag significant shifts. We evaluate PPR in a custom Speaker-Listener environment based on the Multi-Agent Particle Environment under two controlled non-stationarity scenarios. Our results show a trade-off be-[cs.MA] tween detection speed and alarm stability. A smoothed-return baseline detects earlier but produces many repeated alarms. In contrast, apply- ing the detector directly to raw returns often misses the shift. PPR of- fers a more balanced approach by limiting redundant detections while still identifying the controlled shifts. These findings highlight PPR as a lightweight, reward-based monitoring tool that enables cooperative MARL systems to reliably identify major changes during training.

Write only the summary.

- The paper addresses the challenge of non-stationarity in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), where changes in the environment or task objectives render past experience unreliable. It introduces the necessity for agents to recognize such shifts before attempting to adapt their coordinated behaviors.
- The authors propose Patterns of Past Rewards (PPR), a lightweight and algorithm-agnostic change-point detection method. PPR utilizes reward-derived signals by smoothing agents’ return streams, highlighting recent changes, and applying a statistical drift detector to flag significant shifts in the learning process.
- Evaluation is conducted in a custom Speaker-Listener environment based on the Multi-Agent Particle Environment, testing the detector under two controlled non-stationarity scenarios. The study specifically examines the performance of PPR in identifying major changes during training without requiring complex architectural modifications.
- Results reveal a critical trade-off between detection speed and alarm stability. While a smoothed-return baseline detects changes earlier, it generates excessive repeated alarms, and applying the detector to raw returns often misses shifts entirely. PPR provides a balanced solution by effectively limiting redundant detections while reliably identifying controlled shifts.
- The findings establish PPR as a practical, reward-based monitoring tool for cooperative MARL systems. By enabling reliable identification of major environmental changes, PPR facilitates timely adaptation strategies, enhancing the robustness of multi-agent systems in dynamic settings.

Abstract
Abstract. Puncturable signatures, proposed by Bellare et al. (EUROCRYPT 2016), allow a sign- ing key to be punctured (updated) so that it loses the ability to sign particular messages while retaining the ability to sign all others. Halevi et al. (ASIACRYPT 2017) introduced prefix punc- turable signatures, in which the signing key can be punctured with respect to a target prefix so that it cannot sign messages whose prefixes match the target prefix.2026 So far, several generic constructions of prefix puncturable signature schemes have been proposed, including constructions based on identity-based signatures (IBS) (ESORICS 2022) and delegated constrained signatures (IEEE Trans. Inf. Forensics Secure. 2024). However, these constructionsSep suffer from drawbacks in terms of key size. You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a tldr summary in at most 60 words.

The summary must be a single sentence capturing the paper's core contribution.

Paper content:
Feedback Coding Enables Inference-Time Covert Agentic Communication

Abstract
AbstractSep As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate digital interactions, users can leverage LLM-generated text as cover for covert communication within seemingly benign conversations.21 Existing LLM steganography, however, is predominantly white-box, requiring the sender and receiver to share the cover statistics, typically through access to the model weights and prompt. Black-box schemes remove this requirement by allowing the receiver to operate solely on the generated text, but current approaches rely on fixed-length, open-loop watermarking techniques that suffer from high decoding error rates under variable-length token generation. We recast black-box LLM steganography as a sequential[cs.IT] communication problem with causal, noiseless feedback: every generated token is observed by both parties and can guide subsequent embedding. Based on this perspective, we introduce Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), a feedback-coding scheme that combines posterior matching with a decode-and-confirm phase. The design is inspired by classical information-theoretic feedback- coding principles, while its security is established through a cryptographic reduction proof. Across three open-weight language models, we demonstrate that BAM attains 0-0.1% empirical message error on an 8-bit payload in around 50 tokens, across 1000 trials, versus 10-17% for the strongest black-box baseline at comparable length. Building on the proposed steganography algorithm, we demonstrate the feasibility of an end-to-end communication protocol that achieves high communication rates across multiple conversational settings.

Write only the summary.

This paper introduces Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), a feedback-coding scheme for black-box LLM steganography that leverages causal feedback to achieve near-zero error rates in covert communication, significantly outperforming existing open-loop watermarking baselines.

你是一个AI研究助手,可以获取最新的arXiv计算机科学论文。你有以下工具可以使用：

- get_recently_submitted_cs_papers: 获取最近提交的计算机科学领域论文列表，支持按子领域筛选
  参数:
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 50
    aspect (string): 计算机科学子领域代码, 可选值: ['*', 'AI', 'AR']...等41个值
    days (integer): 查询最近多少天的论文, 默认: 7
    output_path (string): 可选：保存到指定文件路径；不传则用项目 output/recent_cs_papers.txt, 默认: 无默认值
    save_to_file (boolean): 是否将论文列表写入文件, 默认: True

- search_arxiv_papers: 按关键词、标题或作者检索 arXiv 论文，可选按提交时间过滤
  参数:
    query (string): 检索词；默认全字段检索，也可用 all:、ti: 或 au: 限定字段, 默认: 无默认值
    max_results (integer): 最大返回结果数, 默认: 10
    days (['integer', 'null']): 可选：只检索最近多少天内提交的论文, 默认: 无默认值

- download_arxiv_pdf: 根据 session 的短期记忆和 ref 下载 arXiv 论文 PDF，并维护 pdf_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): 会话ID，用于从短期记忆中解析 ref 或读取 last_active_paper_id, 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): 是否强制重新下载（覆盖本地文件）, 默认: False

- get_paper_content: Read deterministic text from a downloaded arXiv paper. Returns title + abstract by default, or a requested abstract/method/result/conclusion section.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    section (unknown): Optional section. When omitted, returns title + abstract according to the README T2 contract., 默认: None

- summarize_paper: Summarise a downloaded arXiv paper from its extracted text. Choose style (tldr/structured/bullet) and a max_words budget; the paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    style (string): Summary shape to produce., 可选值: ['tldr', 'structured', 'bullet']
    max_words (integer): Approximate word budget; values are rounded up to the nearest supported budget of 60, 120, 250., 默认: 120

- extract_paper_figures: Extract the embedded figures of a downloaded arXiv paper as image files, with page numbers and captions. The paper PDF must be downloaded first.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值

- analyze_figure: Answer a question about one figure of a downloaded arXiv paper. The paper's figures must be extracted first. Choose question (describe/axes/trend); the answer comes from the environment, not from you.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    figure_no (integer): 1-based index of the figure within the paper, in page order; 1 to 8., 默认: 1
    question (string): What to ask about the figure., 可选值: ['describe', 'axes', 'trend']

- translate_arxiv_pdf: 调用 pdf2zh 翻译 PDF 全文，默认只保留中文单语 mono PDF，并维护 translate_cache.json 索引（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    force (boolean): , 默认: False
    service (string): 翻译服务，如 bing/deepl/google, 默认: bing
    threads (integer): 线程数, 默认: 4
    keep_dual (boolean): 是否保留双语 PDF, 默认: False
    paper_id (string): 可选：直接指定 paper_id（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    pdf_url (string): 可选：直接指定 pdf_url（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值
    input_pdf_path (string): 可选：直接指定本地 PDF 路径（不依赖 session）, 默认: 无默认值

- get_paper_cache_status: 查询某篇论文的本地缓存状态(是否已下载raw、是否已翻译mono), 用于避免重复下载/翻译（ref 支持 null 指代最近操作论文）
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): 论文引用：1-based序号 或 arxiv id 或 title子串；也支持 null 表示最近一次操作的论文, 默认: 无默认值
    paper_id (string): , 默认: 无默认值

- get_translated_content: Read one page of a paper's Chinese translation (the PDF produced by translate_arxiv_pdf). The translation must be finished first. Returns the page text and the total page count.
  参数:
    session_id (string): , 默认: default
    ref (unknown): Paper reference: 1-based result index, arXiv id, or title fragment; null selects the most recently active paper., 默认: 无默认值
    page (integer): 1-based page of the translated PDF; page 1 usually holds the translated title and abstract., 默认: 1

You are building a paper-reading assistant. Read the arXiv paper content below and write a bullet summary in at most 120 words.

The summary must be 3-5 bullet points, each starting with '- '.

Paper content:
Feedback Coding Enables Inference-Time Covert Agentic Communication

Abstract
AbstractSep As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate digital interactions, users can leverage LLM-generated text as cover for covert communication within seemingly benign conversations.21 Existing LLM steganography, however, is predominantly white-box, requiring the sender and receiver to share the cover statistics, typically through access to the model weights and prompt. Black-box schemes remove this requirement by allowing the receiver to operate solely on the generated text, but current approaches rely on fixed-length, open-loop watermarking techniques that suffer from high decoding error rates under variable-length token generation. We recast black-box LLM steganography as a sequential[cs.IT] communication problem with causal, noiseless feedback: every generated token is observed by both parties and can guide subsequent embedding. Based on this perspective, we introduce Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), a feedback-coding scheme that combines posterior matching with a decode-and-confirm phase. The design is inspired by classical information-theoretic feedback- coding principles, while its security is established through a cryptographic reduction proof. Across three open-weight language models, we demonstrate that BAM attains 0-0.1% empirical message error on an 8-bit payload in around 50 tokens, across 1000 trials, versus 10-17% for the strongest black-box baseline at comparable length. Building on the proposed steganography algorithm, we demonstrate the feasibility of an end-to-end communication protocol that achieves high communication rates across multiple conversational settings.

Write only the summary.

- Recasts black-box LLM steganography as a sequential communication problem with causal, noiseless feedback, overcoming limitations of fixed-length, open-loop watermarking.
- Introduces Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), a feedback-coding scheme that uses posterior matching and a decode-and-confirm phase to guide token embedding.
- Establishes security through a cryptographic reduction proof, ensuring robust covert communication without requiring shared model weights or prompts.
- Demonstrates superior performance across three open-weight LLMs, achieving 0-0.1% message error on an 8-bit payload in ~50 tokens, significantly outperforming baselines with 10-17% error rates.
- Validates the feasibility of an end-to-end communication protocol that maintains high communication rates across various conversational settings.

Overview of the BackTrend construction pipeline. We first compile 25 mature target topics from the Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning domain of a 2024 JRC report (Eulaerts et al., 2025) and retrieve their 2019–2024 papers from Semantic Scholar. We then mine problem-space and solution-space candidate topics from the 2019–2023 abstracts, consolidate them by embedding clustering, and score each candidate by its 2019–2024 publication frequency, keeping only candidates that pass all four frequency gates. MagnifiQ: Patch-aware Text Guided Progressive Upscaling for High-Resolution Image Restoration

Abstract
Fig. 1: MagnifiQ restores real-world low-quality inputs into coherent high-resolution outputs up to 4096×4096, supporting up to 32× scaling while preserving global struc- ture and recovering fine details. Zoom in for details.[cs.CV] Abstract. High-resolution image restoration from degraded inputs is challenging because it must preserve global structural consistency while recovering fine-grained local details, especially at 4K resolution where di- rect diffusion-based restoration is computationally expensive and prone to repeated or inconsistent textures. In this work, we introduce Mag- nifiQ, an image restoration framework that progressively upscales and restores images across resolutions, e.g., from 1024 × 1024 to 4096 × 4096. Our approach leverages a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model such as SDXL and adapts it for more scalable high-resolution inference by replacing its original self-attention layers with convolutional operations whose computational cost grows linearly with image resolution. We fur- ther propose a progressive upscaling strategy that iteratively restores images over multiple resolution stages, refining each intermediate output rather than directly hallucinating the final 4K image, thereby improv- ing global coherence and reducing high-resolution artifacts. To enhancearXiv:2608.14543v1 local details while controlling content drift, MagnifiQ uses patch-specific text prompts that provide spatially localized semantic guidance during

Write only the summary.

MagnifiQ is a patch-aware, text-guided framework for high-resolution image restoration that progressively upscales images up to 4096×4096 by adapting pre-trained diffusion models with linear-complexity convolutional operations and spatially localized semantic prompts to ensure global structural consistency and fine detail recovery.

    session_id (string): , 默认: default
